answer: The amount payable is the Event of Default Redemption Amount, which for 'Amortised Face Amount' is the amount calculated under Condition 3(b): the scheduled Zero Coupon Note Redemption Amount on the Maturity Date discounted at the Amortisation Yield (per annum, compounded annually); for periods under one year, using the Day Count Fraction in the Final Terms. If not paid when due, the same calculation continues using the Relevant Date in place of the Maturity Date (until the Relevant Date, unless it falls on/after the Maturity Date, in which case the scheduled redemption amount plus accruing interest is due). It is payable together with accrued interest to the date of payment. The triggering event: a dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer under Belgian law (bankruptcy, judicial liquidation or voluntary liquidation other than in connection with a reconstruction/merger/amalgamation where the continuing corporation assumes all liabilities); each Noteholder of the relevant Series may then give written notice to the Paying Agent that its Notes are immediately repayable. (A payment default continuing 30+ days only lets a holder institute dissolution/liquidation proceedings in Belgium; it does not itself give the right to accelerate; resolution action by the Resolution Authority does not entitle acceleration.)
